modern: If you take away your opinion about what seems to give you pain, you yourself stand in perfect security.—Who is this self?—Reason.—But I am not reason.—So be it. Then let the reason itself not trouble itself. But if any other part of you suffers, let it have its own opinion about itself.
original: If thou takest away thy opinion about that which appears to give thee pain, thou thyself standest in perfect security.—Who is this self?—The reason.—But I am not reason.—Be it so. Let then the reason itself not trouble itself. But if any other part of thee suffers, let it have its own opinion about itself.
